newsitem.title: UK: Official reprimand for UK judge who said "nigger".
newsitem.headline: Official reprimand for UK judge who said "nigger".

text.p: The British government's leading law official reprimanded a judge on Wednesday for using the phrase "people...who work like niggers" during a court case.
"Remarks of this kind do wholly disproportionate damage to the perception of justice and the reputation of the judiciary," said the Lord Chancellor, Lord Mackay, in a statement.

It is not the first time Judge William Crawford has had a run-in with the Lord Chancellor. He was publicly rebuked for hugging and kissing a blonde court usher in 1992 in what was described as an "over-familiar greeting".
After the incident the British popular press dubbed him "Zorro" on account of his swashbuckling good looks.
Crawford made the offending comment at Newcastle Crown Court, in northern England, on March 7, when a woman said she could not do community service work due to an ulcer.
Crawford snapped that he knew many people with ulcers who worked "like niggers", causing outrage in the public gallery.
The antiquated expression meaning to work hard is the equivalent of the modern phrase "to work like a dog".
Although the Lord Chancellor found the language "wrong and regrettable", he saw that it may have been a momentary lapse.
"I trust you now recognise that use of such expressions is likely to give offence...to members of ethnic minorities," the Lord Chancellor wrote to the judge.
Crawford issued a public apology on March 12 saying the comment was "a regrettable slip" with no offence intended and he did not want to be thought of as a racist.
Last year the Court of Appeal established a precedent for the Lord Chancellor's rebuke, dictating that the word "nigger" could no longer be used without giving offence.
